name: TRX Y-Fly
notes: Face the anchor holding the handles with straight arms in front of you, body leaning back in one straight line. Pull the shoulder blades down and back, then raise the arms up and out into a Y over your head, thumbs up. Your body comes up with the arms; don't bend the elbows or arch the low back. Lower slowly.
settingHarder: Walk your feet closer to the anchor (lean back more)
settingEasier: Step back so you're more upright
why: Trabaja trapecio inferior y estabilizadores de la escápula, que en escaladores suelen estar débiles frente al dorsal. Ayuda a prevenir dolor de hombro en techos y bloqueos altos.

name: TRX T-Fly
notes: Face the anchor holding the handles with straight arms in front of your chest, leaning back with the body straight. Squeeze the shoulder blades together and open the arms out to the sides into a T until your hands are in line with your shoulders. Keep the elbows almost straight and the ribs down. Return slowly.
settingHarder: Walk your feet closer to the anchor (lean back more)
settingEasier: Step back so you're more upright
why: Deltoides posterior y romboides: el lado de la espalda que la escalada casi no trabaja. Mejora la postura de hombros (hombros adelante).

name: TRX Face Pull
notes: Face the anchor with palms facing down, arms straight, leaning back. Pull the handles toward your forehead, elbows high and wide, and finish by rotating the forearms up so the hands end beside your ears (a W shape). Hold one second, then lower slowly with control.
settingHarder: Walk your feet closer to the anchor (lean back more)
settingEasier: Step back so you're more upright
why: Combina retracción escapular con rotación externa del hombro (manguito rotador). Es de los ejercicios de 'prehab' más recomendados para escaladores.

name: TRX Row
notes: Face the anchor, hold the handles with straight arms and lean back with the body in one straight line from heels to head. Start by pulling the shoulder blades back, then pull your chest to the handles, elbows close to the body. Lower slowly until the arms are straight again. Don't let the hips sag.
settingHarder: Walk your feet closer to the anchor (body more horizontal)
settingEasier: Step back so you're more upright
why: Tirón horizontal con control escapular; equilibra el volumen de tirón vertical de la escalada. Ojo: ya existe 'Inverted Row' en la librería, puede ser el mismo.

name: TRX Power Pull
notes: Hold one handle with one hand, facing the anchor, and lean back. Let the free arm reach toward the anchor and the torso rotate open toward the working side. Pull with the working arm while rotating the chest back toward the anchor, and finish with the free arm reaching behind you. Control the way back down.
settingHarder: Walk your feet closer to the anchor
settingEasier: Step back so you're more upright
why: Tirón a un brazo con rotación de tronco: parecido a los movimientos de bloqueo con giro de cadera en la pared.

name: TRX Biceps Curl
notes: Face the anchor with palms up, arms straight and the body leaning back. Keeping the elbows high and still at shoulder height, bend the elbows and bring the hands toward your forehead. The body moves; the elbows don't drop. Lower slowly.
settingHarder: Walk your feet closer to the anchor (lean back more)
settingEasier: Step back so you're more upright
why: Bíceps y braquial con carga ajustable y suave para el codo. Útil para fortalecer el codo o volver de una molestia.

name: TRX Push-up
notes: Face away from the anchor with the feet in the foot cradles (hard) or hands in the handles (easier). Keep the body in a straight plank, lower the chest between the hands with elbows at about 45°, then push back up. Don't let the straps rub your arms or the hips sag.
settingHarder: Feet in the straps, hands on the floor; or hands in the straps with feet further back
settingEasier: Hands in the straps and walk your feet toward the anchor (more upright)
why: Antagonistas (pecho, tríceps, serrato) con inestabilidad: protege el hombro y equilibra tanto tirón.

name: TRX Triceps Extension
notes: Face away from the anchor holding the handles with the arms straight overhead, leaning forward with the body straight. Bend only at the elbows, lowering the head between the hands, then straighten the arms to come back up. Keep the elbows pointing forward and the core tight.
settingHarder: Walk your feet back (lean forward more)
settingEasier: Step forward so you're more upright
why: Tríceps: antagonista clave para el codo del escalador (epicondilitis). Carga fácil de ajustar.

name: TRX Knee Tuck
notes: Start in a high plank with the feet in the foot cradles, hands under the shoulders. Pull the knees toward the chest by rounding the low back slightly, then push the legs back out to a straight plank. Keep the shoulders over the hands and move slowly.
settingHarder: Move the hands further from the anchor; or go to TRX Pike
settingEasier: Hands closer to the anchor; smaller range
why: Core anterior con piernas suspendidas: transfiere a mantener los pies en la pared en desplomes.

name: TRX Pike
notes: Start in a high plank with the feet in the foot cradles. Keeping the legs straight, lift the hips high toward the ceiling until you're in an upside-down V, shoulders over the hands. Lower slowly back to the plank without letting the hips drop below the line.
settingHarder: Hands further from the anchor; add a push-up at the bottom
why: Compresión de cadera y core fuerte, como subir los pies alto en un desplome.

name: TRX Body Saw
notes: Get into a forearm plank with the feet in the foot cradles. Keeping the body rigid, push yourself backward from the forearms so the shoulders move past the elbows, then pull back forward. Small range, slow, no sagging hips.
why: Anti-extensión del core: mantener el cuerpo rígido con los brazos lejos, como en movimientos largos.

name: TRX Fallout
notes: Face away from the anchor holding the handles with straight arms in front of you, leaning forward. Keeping the arms straight and the body in one line, let the arms rise overhead as you fall forward, then pull the arms back down to return. Stop before the low back arches.
settingHarder: Walk your feet back (lean forward more)
settingEasier: Step forward so you're more upright
why: Rollout de pie: core y dorsal trabajando juntos, como sostener tensión en presas lejanas.

name: TRX Side Plank
notes: Put both feet in the foot cradles, top foot in front of the bottom one, and lie on your side on one forearm, elbow under the shoulder. Lift the hips until the body is straight from head to feet and hold. Don't let the hips drop or rotate.
settingHarder: Add hip dips or a top-arm reach-through
why: Core lateral y oblicuos; da estabilidad en posiciones de lado (dropknees, contraposiciones).

name: TRX Hamstring Curl
notes: Lie on your back with the heels in the foot cradles under the anchor. Lift the hips into a bridge, then pull the heels toward your glutes while keeping the hips high. Straighten the legs slowly, still keeping the hips up.
settingEasier: Keep the hips down on the curl
why: Isquiotibiales en flexión de rodilla: es exactamente el gesto del heel hook. Previene lesiones de isquios.

name: TRX Bulgarian Split Squat
notes: Face away from the anchor and put one foot in a foot cradle behind you. Hop the front foot forward and lower the back knee toward the floor, keeping the front knee over the toes and the chest tall. Push through the front heel to stand. Finish all reps, then switch legs.
settingEasier: Shorter range; hold on to a post
why: Pierna a una pierna con equilibrio: fuerza para empujar con una pierna en pasos altos.

name: TRX Lat Stretch
notes: Hold both handles (or one, for one side) with straight arms, facing the anchor. Step back and sit the hips back and down, letting the arms go overhead and the chest drop until you feel a stretch along the side of the back and armpit. Breathe and let the body hang into it.
why: Estira dorsal y hombro, que se acortan con mucho tirón. Buen cierre de sesión.
